official.deadline_note: The central deadline is the Mobility-Online cut-off. The binding date for an applicant is the internal deadline of the host institution that nominates them, which runs earlier: for the 2026-2027 round KU Leuven 15 January 2026, University of Antwerp 1 February 2026, AP 1 March 2026, HOGENT 20 March 2026, LUCA School of Arts 1 April 2026, Ghent University 1 April 2026, VUB 1 April 2026, Hasselt University 15 March 2026, Erasmus Brussels 13 April 2026. For the 2027-2028 round KU Leuven has published an institutional deadline of 15 January 2027; no 2027-2028 central deadline has been published by VLUHR yet.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 (last published call, closed); 2027-2028 round not yet launched and under Ministry review
official.status_note: VLUHR publishes the call for the academic year 2026-2027 as closed. The page warns that the scholarship is currently under review by the Ministry of Education and that the awarded grant, selection process, criteria and modalities may change for the academic year 2027-2028. KU Leuven, as a host institution, has already published a preliminary 2027-2028 Master Mind route (applications open 15 October 2026, deadline 15 January 2027) explicitly marked preliminary and subject to change, pending confirmation no later than January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Host institution can ask the applicant for a tuition fee that equals the lowest rate of the yearly tuition fee for a student who receives a study grant from the Flemish Government. The rate for the academic year 2026-2027 is EUR 136,50. This rate may increase slightly from year to year.
benefits: A maximum scholarship of EUR 10.225 per academic year
Tuition fee waiver: the host institution can only charge the lowest study-grant tariff, EUR 136,50 for 2026-2027
Duration of mobility: one academic year for a 60 ECTS master programme, two academic years for a 120 ECTS master programme
Reserved scholarships for priority countries: Japan (3), Mexico (3), Palestine (2) and USA (5)
Total programme budget of EUR 480.000 for 2026-2027, an estimated 30 international students benefitting
A maximum of 20 applications can be submitted per Flemish higher education institution
eligibility: The applicant applies to take up a Master degree programme at a Flemish higher education institution (Host institution).
A Grade Point Average of 3.5 out of 4.0, calculated on the last obtained Bachelor's or Master's degree.
Good knowledge of English, with proof no older than 3 years at the time of application processing by the host institution (April).
All nationalities, except for Russian, can apply.

Students already enrolled in a Flemish higher education institution cannot apply; the only exception is international students already enrolled in a specific preparatory programme when applying in spring to start a master's in September.

The previous degree for which the student is approved for the master programme must not have been obtained at a Flemish institution; students who did credit mobility at a hosting Flemish institution remain eligible.
The applicant can be nominated by only one Flemish higher education institution and must choose one if preselected by more.
Preparatory programmes, bridging programmes and distance learning are not eligible.
At least half of the credits of the master programme must be obtained at the Flemish host institution.
requirements: An overall band score of minimum 7.0 on the IELTS test (IELTS Indicator accepted), or a minimum total score of 94 on TOEFL (TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition accepted), a C1 level of the CEFR, or a similar result in another official language test recognised by the host institution.

Applicants for a Master programme at a School of Arts: at least an overall band score of 6.5 on IELTS, a minimum total score of 90 on TOEFL, a B2 level of the CEFR, or a similar result in another official English language test recognised by the host institution.

The host institution performs an academic check of the file and the student must be accepted by the host institution to receive the scholarship, even if that decision comes after the Master Mind selection.

In case of a two-year Master programme at least 54 ECTS must be obtained in the first academic year to receive the final instalment of the first year and to be entitled to the scholarship for the second year.
Upon completion of the mobility, students are expected to submit an essay for which a format is provided and to fill in a short questionnaire about their mobility.
documents: Copy of the international passport or national ID
A Curriculum Vitae including the American GPA out of 4.0 and, if applicable, publications, academic awards and previous scholarships
Transcript of records (certified translation required if not written in Dutch, French, German or English)
English language test results or a letter of exemption provided by the host university
Letter of motivation written in English
Two signed letters of recommendation from professors of the previous home university, university of applied sciences, school of Arts or a recent employer, written in English
Copy of acquired diploma(s) (certified translation required if not written in Dutch, French, German or English)
Three reasons of motivation for submission, at least 150 words, formulated in English by the host institution and uploaded by the host institution
selection_criteria: Quality of the applicant's motivation: 30 points
Previous study results in the transcript of records: 30 points
Reasons for recommending the applicant in recommendation letter 1: 10 points
Reasons for recommending the applicant in recommendation letter 2: 10 points
Motivation for submission by the host institution: 10 points
Top talent profile of the applicant: 10 points
Each application is read by two independent jury members; files are reopened where scores differ by more than 10% and a final consolidated ranking is produced.
coverage: Grant of EUR 10.225 per academic year, paid in instalments: EUR 4.600 on arrival with the registration certificate (optionally EUR 2.000 before the start of the year plus EUR 2.600 on arrival), EUR 4.100 in February upon completion of the first semester, and EUR 1.525 on completion of the academic year
Two-year programme: EUR 6.125 before the start of the second academic year, EUR 4.100 in February of the second year, EUR 1.525 on completion of the second year
Tuition fee waiver; only the lowest study-grant tariff of EUR 136,50 for 2026-2027 remains payable to the host institution
No travel, installation or insurance allowance is published in the payment schedule
application_method: Step 1: the applicant submits his/her application to the host institution, whose internal deadline may differ from the central one.
Step 2: the host institution accepts the application of the candidate.
Step 3: the host institution starts the Master Mind procedure by creating the candidate's application file in the Mobility-Online tool.
Step 4: the applicant receives an email from Mobility-Online notifying them of being preselected.
Step 5: the applicant registers in Mobility-Online and completes the application file before the deadline, uploading all required documents.
Step 6: the host institution validates and submits the completed file in Mobility-Online before the central deadline; files submitted after the deadline are not accepted.
official.application_route: Apply to a participating Flemish host institution first; the institution screens, nominates and opens the file in Mobility-Online, and the applicant then completes and validates it before the central deadline. Applicants cannot self-nominate.
official.citizenship_residency: All nationalities, except for Russian, can apply. No residency requirement.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, the programme targets international students; students already enrolled at a Flemish higher education institution are excluded apart from the narrow preparatory-programme exception.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any Master programme at a participating Flemish university, School of Arts or the Antwerp Maritime Academy, excluding preparatory, bridging and distance-learning programmes; at least half of the credits must be earned at the host institution.
official.duration: One academic year for a 60 ECTS master programme and two academic years for a 120 ECTS master programme
official.description: The Flemish Ministry of Education and Training awards scholarships to outstanding students for Master programmes in Flanders and Brussels. The programme aims to promote Flanders and Brussels as a top study destination for international talents, with applications accepted from all Flemish universities, Schools of Arts and the Antwerp Maritime Academy.
official.program_type: Master's scholarship (60 or 120 ECTS) funded by the Flemish Ministry of Education and Training, managed by VLUHR
official.english_requirement: Good knowledge of English, with proof no older than 3 years at the time of application processing by the host institution (April): an overall band score of minimum 7.0 on IELTS (IELTS Indicator accepted), a minimum total score of 94 on TOEFL (TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition accepted), a C1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference, or a similar result in another official language test recognised by the host institution. School of Arts applicants: minimum IELTS 6.5, minimum TOEFL 90, or CEFR B2.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a nomination-driven award: you cannot apply directly to the Flemish Government, so your first submission is to a participating host institution and it is that institution's internal deadline, not the central 27 April cut-off, that decides whether you are in the running. Budget for the fact that the €10,225 annual grant is released in instalments tied to your arrival, your first-semester results and actually completing the degree, so the final €1,525 disappears if you do not finish within the year. Treat the €136,50 tuition tariff as the only education cost you keep, and plan your own visa, insurance and travel money separately because nothing is published for those.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-GPA international master's applicants, excluding Russian nationals, who can win a nomination from a Flemish host institution and are willing to run that institution's earlier internal calendar.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your intended Flemish institution actually participates and write its internal scholarship deadline into your calendar before anything else
Convert your last degree to the US-style GPA out of 4.0 that VLUHR uses, using the Scholaro calculator they link, before you assume you clear the 3.5 bar
Book an accepted English test early enough that the result is still under 3 years old when the host institution processes files in April
Ask two referees for signed English letters well before the host institution's deadline - they carry 20 of the 100 selection points
Get certified translations ready for any transcript or diploma not in Dutch, French, German or English
Chase the host institution for the 150-word three-reasons-of-motivation document they must upload on your behalf, and make sure your file is validated in Mobility-Online before the central deadline
Check that your degree was not obtained at a Flemish institution and that you are not already enrolled in Flanders
common_rejection_risks: Missing the host institution's internal deadline, which means no nomination and no Mobility-Online file at all
A GPA that falls short of 3.5 out of 4.0 on the recalculated US scale, or study results that carry too few of the 30 transcript points
Enrolling in a preparatory, bridging or distance-learning programme, which is excluded outright
Being preselected by two Flemish institutions and failing to choose a single one
Weak host-institution submission motivation and thin recommendation letters, which together decide 30 of the 100 points
Failing to obtain 54 ECTS in the first year of a 120 ECTS programme, which cancels the second year of funding
Holding any Flemish Government, Erasmus+/Erasmus Mundus, BAEF or Fulbright scholarship, which makes the combination illegal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 136,50 minimum tuition tariff, visa and residence-permit costs, health insurance, travel to Belgium and all living costs beyond the EUR 10,225 annual grant. No travel, installation or insurance allowance is published.
document_audit: Certified translations are mandatory for transcripts and diplomas that are not in Dutch, French, German or English
The English test must be under 3 years old in April, when the host institution processes the file, not on the day you apply
Your CV has to state the GPA out of 4.0 explicitly, so compute it rather than pasting your local grading scale
The three reasons of motivation are written and uploaded by the host institution, so an unresponsive international office can stall your file
A profile picture and a passport or national ID copy are compulsory uploads inside Mobility-Online
Recommendation letters must be signed and in English, from professors of your previous institution or a recent employer
alerts: Russian nationals are excluded from applying, with no exception
The final EUR 1,525 instalment is withheld if the master's degree is not obtained in July, or September in the case of re-sit examinations
Discontinuing the programme early forces a partial repayment of the grant, keeping only the instalment matching the time completed
The Ministry of Education is reviewing the whole programme, so the grant, criteria and modalities for 2027-2028 may differ from the published 2026-2027 terms
KU Leuven's 2027-2028 Master Mind page is explicitly preliminary and subject to confirmation no later than January 2027
An essay and a mobility questionnaire are obligatory after the mobility ends
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You apply to a participating Flemish host institution first; it nominates you and opens your Mobility-Online file, you complete and validate the uploads before the central deadline, and the Flemish Selection Committee ranks files in May with results at the end of May.

official.deadline_note: KU Leuven publishes a single 15 January deadline that applies to both the master's programme application file and the separate scholarship candidacy registration; no earlier institutional scholarship deadline is published. Applications open 15 October 2026.
official.status_note: The 2027-2028 page, last updated 5 October 2026, states that applications open on 15 October 2026 and close at 23.59 CET on 15 January 2027. The 2026-2027 round, which closed on 15 January 2026, is finished.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship holders receive a full tuition fee waiver and pay only an annual administration fee of circa EUR 140.
benefits: Scholarship type: full fee waiver and allowance
Incoming students will receive a scholarship of EUR 13,200 per academic year, for a maximum of two academic years
Full tuition fee waiver with only an annual administration fee of circa EUR 140 remaining payable
One scholarship is available for the academic year 2027-2028

Automatic consideration through the same application for the Master Mind Scholarship, the KU Leuven ASEAN Scholarship, the KU Leuven Scholarship for Africa and the KU Leuven Scholarship for Central and South America
eligibility: Study level: master's programmes at KU Leuven.
The student has a high level of academic performance and potential, with excellent study results reflected in a high Grade Point Average on the transcript of records.

Previous degree(s) should have been obtained at a higher education institution outside Flanders; international students who have completed a credit mobility programme at a host Flemish higher education institution remain eligible.

Students already enrolled at a Flemish higher education institution are not eligible; the only exception is international students who, when applying for a scholarship in the spring, are enrolled in a specific preparatory programme to start their master's programme in September.

Students are not allowed to combine the Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship with another full scholarship offered by KU Leuven, the national or regional governments of Belgium, or the European Commission.
Applicants whose first language is not English must demonstrate a good knowledge and command of English.
Students enrolled in bridging programmes or distance learning programmes are not eligible.

KU Leuven Scholarships & Master Mind Candidacy Form for academic year 2027-2028, uploaded under the document type 'Annexe'

One-minute motivational video, required only after nomination by the programme

coverage: Full tuition fee waiver for the eligible master's programme, with only an annual administration fee of circa EUR 140 remaining payable
Scholarship of EUR 13,200 per academic year, for a maximum of two academic years
Duration of one academic year for a 60 ECTS master's programme and two academic years for a 120 ECTS master's programme

official.citizenship_residency: All nationalities are eligible. No residency requirement.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, all nationalities are eligible; students already enrolled at a Flemish higher education institution are excluded apart from the preparatory-programme exception.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The target programme must be on KU Leuven's published eligible master's programmes list for 2027-2028; bridging programmes and distance learning programmes are not eligible.
official.duration: One academic year for a 60 ECTS master's programme and two academic years for a 120 ECTS master's programme; the allowance runs for a maximum of two academic years
official.description: Financed by donations to the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund, the Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship is a fully-funded scholarship for outstanding students, available for all master's and advanced master's programmes at KU Leuven, built on the University's baseline of inspiring the outstanding through high academic standards, innovative research, global engagement and societal impact.
official.program_type: Master's scholarship financed by the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund
official.english_requirement: Applicants whose first language is not English must demonstrate a good knowledge and command of English; KU Leuven's English proficiency tests page lists the accepted admission tests and minima: TOEFL iBT overall 79, IELTS Academic overall 6.5, Cambridge English Advanced (C1) or Proficiency (C2), or ITACE C1/C2. Duolingo scores, MyBest and One Skill Retake composites are not accepted. Students who previously completed an English-taught programme in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the United States are exempt. The 2026-2027 scholarship page published higher scholarship-specific minima of Online TOEFL 94, IELTS 7 or Cambridge CPE C2.

applicant_utility.summary: The realistic way to treat this award is as a free extra lottery ticket attached to a master's application you were going to make anyway: the same single application automatically puts you forward for the Master Mind Scholarship and the KU Leuven ASEAN, Africa and Central and South America scholarships, so you are effectively competing for five prizes on one form. Remember there is only one Inspiring the Outstanding award for 2027-2028, so it should never be the pillar of your funding plan, but the Master Mind route it unlocks carries roughly EUR 10,750 at KU Leuven and is far more attainable. Take an accepted English test before the 15 January 2027 deadline, since the test date itself must precede the cut-off even though you may upload the result afterwards.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Outstanding international master's applicants whose previous degree was earned outside Flanders, who want one KU Leuven application to reach five scholarships and can hit a genuinely strong academic record.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify that your target programme appears on KU Leuven's eligible master's programmes list for 2027-2028 before you invest in the application
Download the academic-year 2027-2028 Candidacy Form and upload it in the application tool under the document type 'Annexe' - it is not part of the standard degree file
Register the scholarship candidacy in the separate online registration tool; finishing the programme application alone does not enter you
Book an accepted English test now so it is taken before 15 January 2027, and make the result available for online verification
Record a one-minute motivational video in advance so a nomination on 10 March does not catch you with a 6 March scramble
Check the combination rule if you already hold or expect any KU Leuven, Belgian government or European Commission full scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Treating a one-award scholarship as a realistic sole funding source when the odds are extremely low
A previous degree already obtained at a Flemish institution, which makes you ineligible outright
Applying for a programme that is not on the eligible list, or for a bridging or distance-learning programme
Leaving the separate candidacy registration undone while assuming the programme application covers it
Relying on an English test taken after the deadline, or on a score KU Leuven does not accept
Assuming silence means your file is still pending - the university announces the end of nominations and gives no personal feedback
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The circa EUR 140 annual administration fee, plus all living costs beyond the EUR 13,200 yearly allowance. No travel or installation allowance is published, so flights, visa and insurance are entirely on you.
document_audit: The Candidacy Form annexe is a mandatory upload with its own document type in the application tool; the degree file alone is not a scholarship application
